subject.title: [Feature Request]: Session snapshots — save and load context checkpoints (/session save|load)

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-class core session snapshot workflow, and which first shipped semantics should it own: named save/load checkpoints, archive restore, branch/fork, deterministic replay, or a narrower resume-only path?
rationale: The code already has partial primitives, but the remaining behavior crosses user-facing commands, persistent session state, destructive restore behavior, archive import, prompt-cache expectations, and protocol/API shape, so automation cannot safely pick the product contract.

options.title: Design core snapshots first
options.body: Keep this issue open as the broad design item and specify save/list/load/branch/restore semantics before implementation.

options.title: Narrow to resume-only
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/82684 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/86829 as the immediate path for past-session resume while leaving named snapshots out of scope.

options.title: Defer native snapshots
options.body: Close or park the broader snapshot direction until a smaller plugin/API or storage migration proposal proves the missing core seam.

recommendation.title: Design core snapshots first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the broad design item and specify save/list/load/branch/restore semantics before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across session management, compaction checkpoints, docs, and the visible issue follow-up.
